newsitem.title: LATVIA: HOTEL LATVIA SELL-OFF RULES APPROVED.
newsitem.headline: HOTEL LATVIA SELL-OFF RULES APPROVED.

text.p: The Privatisation Agency (LPA) has set the sell-off rules for the Hotel Latvia, which will take place in three stages, the agency said on Thursday.
The Latvia, which has 354 rooms and 691 beds, had turnover of 2.37 million lats and profit of 8,700 lats in 1996.
After the privatisation, the share capital of the Latvia, the biggest hotel in Riga, will reach 3.1 million lats versus a current 2.1 million lats, said LPA official Raimonds Ozols.
The first stage, the making the hotel into a state joint stock company, was completed in April.

Attracting private investors via an issue of one million shares to take the share capital to 3.1 million lats is the second stage and the third is selling the state's stake or 2.09 million shares with a nominal value of one lats.
More than 10 investors have applied to take part in the second stage and a tender for new issue and the rules for this sell-off stage will be approved at the end of June.
Any strategic investor will have to invest 25 million lats in the hotel over the next three years.
Ozols said that 30 percent of the state's share will be sold in a public offer, expected this autumn.
Some 14 percent of the state's stake will be offered to employees and pensioners and 9.5 percent will be included in the Savings Bank (Krajbanka) restructuring programme.
A package of 38 percent of the state's stake will also be offered to the strategic investor who took part in the issue of new shares and who will have first right of refusal.
Latvia registered an off-season first quarter loss of 45,000 lats but saw results improving at the end of May.
"Judging by the first five month results, which show an upward trend, the tourism industry has begun picking up again," Kalninsh added.
Half of the rooms have been renovated in the last few years to reach four-star standards, said manager Janis Kalninsh.
